headline_marked: Tk 12.86cr project: [[Riverbank embankment collapses]] within two months in Faridpur
headline: Tk 12.86cr project: Riverbank embankment collapses within two months in Faridpur
summary: An 80-metre stretch of a riverbank protection project along the Madhumati river collapsed shortly after handover, raising concerns over construction quality.
details: An 80-metre stretch of a riverbank protection embankment in Faridpur’s Alfadanga has collapsed within two months of being handed over to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).
The damaged section is part of a 280-metre embankment in the Char Azampur area of Tagarband union along the Madhumati river, built at a cost of Tk 12.86 crore.
The structure began caving in on August 30, with erosion continuing until September 15. A total of 80 metres of the protection work collapsed into the river.
The collapse has caused significant loss for locals, including the washing away of a resident's kitchen and the loss of ancestral graves and land.
A local UP member alleged that the contractor failed to lay supporting stones deep enough in the river, instead using sandbags pushed into the river with excavators.
Md Rakib Hossain, executive engineer of BWDB Faridpur, stated that the contractor's security money has been withheld and he has been directed to repair the damaged section promptly.
The contractor, Kabirul Islam Siddiqui, denied poor construction quality, blaming the collapse on a char deflecting the river current towards the bank.
caption:
A Tk 12.86 crore embankment project collapsed in just two months. How did this happen?

An 80-metre stretch of a riverbank protection embankment in Faridpur’s Alfadanga has collapsed within two months of being handed over to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).

The damaged section is part of a 280-metre embankment in the Char Azampur area of Tagarband union along the Madhumati river, built at a cost of Tk 12.86 crore.

The structure began caving in on August 30, with erosion continuing until September 15. A total of 80 metres of the protection work collapsed into the river.

The collapse has caused significant loss for locals, including the washing away of a resident's kitchen and the loss of ancestral graves and land.

A local UP member alleged that the contractor failed to lay supporting stones deep enough in the river, instead using sandbags pushed into the river with excavators.

Md Rakib Hossain, executive engineer of BWDB Faridpur, stated that the contractor's security money has been withheld and he has been directed to repair the damaged section promptly.

The contractor, Kabirul Islam Siddiqui, denied poor construction quality, blaming the collapse on a char deflecting the river current towards the bank.
